final.title: Why reviewer training is not enough
final.body:
Reviewer training helps, but it is only one control. If the same approval logic is used again and again, the bigger problem is often not knowledge. It is repeatable steps, data entry, fatigue, or edge cases. Training can improve judgment; it does not change the workflow itself.

The practical question is simple: are the errors mainly coming from people not knowing the rule, or from a process that still depends on manual checking every time? If it is the second case, you are looking at a workflow decision, not a classroom problem.

A plain example: if the same approval rules are applied to every transaction, a tired reviewer can still miss one step. A repeatable rule check can catch that kind of miss. A slide deck cannot. That is not a complaint about people. It is just how Friday afternoons work.

At Bareni, we focus on repeatable logic steps in small-business workflows, with human approval kept for exceptions and high-risk decisions. That is a policy choice, not a guarantee.

So the next step is to identify one recurring decision step that follows the same logic each time and note how often it appears. If it is truly repeatable, it is worth separating from reviewer training before you spend more time on materials.
